# Colocalisation of an index credible set and a list of credible sets generated by query_ot() or query_eqtl_cat()

Note that the two credible sets are matched by column "snp". Therefore
it is important that the formatting of the snp column in cs matches that
in the object returned by query_ot(). It can be helpful to examine that
object as shown in the example below.

## Usage

``` r
coloc_query(cs, querylist)
```

## Arguments

- cs:

  index credible set: a data.frame containing columns "snp" (character)
  and "PP" (numeric). "snp" will be used to match against credible sets
  in querylist and should be of the format "chr_pos_ref_alt", eg
  "6_90279406_G_C" (not "chr6_90279406_G_C").

- querylist:

  output of query_ot() or query_eqtl_cat(). If querylist is of length 0
  (no credible sets), this function warns and returns NULL.

## Value

a data.frame containing coloc results, one row per credible set in
querylist, with the annotation from querylist

## Details

This function uses the coloc_pip method for colocalisation.

## See also

[`query_ot()`](https://chr1swallace.github.io/coloc/reference/query_ot.md),
[`query_eqtl_cat()`](https://chr1swallace.github.io/coloc/reference/query_eqtl_cat.md),
[`coloc_pip()`](https://chr1swallace.github.io/coloc/reference/coloc_pip.md)

## Author

Chris Wallace

## Examples

``` r
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
q <- data.frame(chr = 6,
   pos = c(90279406, 90280331, 90281412, 90276601, 90288603, 90286261),
   snp = c("6_90279406_G_C", "6_90280331_G_A", "6_90281412_A_T",
           "6_90276601_A_G", "6_90288603_A_G", "6_90286261_C_G"),
   PP = c(0.675, 0.0747, 0.0702, 0.0505, 0.0422, 0.0412))

ot <- query_ot(q)
head(ot[[1]]) # check the snp format matches that in q
head(q)
out <- coloc_query(q, ot)
out[out$PP.H4 > 0 & out$studyType != "gwas", ]
} # }
```
